notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).

name: VISTA: An End-to-End Benchmark for Visual Spec-to-Web-App Coding Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent GUI-application generation benchmark with real component interaction probes; its main evaluated agents are application coders, not general GUI task executors.

name: GUI Agents for Continual Game Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. GUI agents actually load and play browser-game builds, providing an executable interface-testing signal for game-code generation; the central application remains game development.

name: CLI-Anything: Towards Agent-Native Computer Use
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent computer-interface architecture: the described application command harnesses concern computer operation, but no GUI execution or comparative benchmark result is established in the abstract.
summary: CLI-Anything argues for application interfaces built around structured commands, explicit state and execution feedback. It describes transforming existing software into command-line harnesses and organizing that approach through CLI-Hub.

name: AppAgent-Claw: CLI Is All You Need for GUI Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces AppAgent-Claw, which records demonstrated GUI workflows as reusable OpenClaw skills, locates visual targets during replay and checks intended on-screen effects.

name: Syll: Open-Source Personal Automation with Cross-Surface Execution
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Syll combines tool calls, shell execution and visual GUI control in a personal-automation runtime. It turns user demonstrations into reusable skills and exposes execution logs, keyframes and approval checkpoints for inspection.

name: ComAct: Reframing Professional Software Manipulation via COM-as-Action Paradigm
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ComAct proposes COM program synthesis as an alternative interface for manipulating professional software and introduces ComCADBench with GUI-based comparison agents. ComActor adds a staged training and correction approach, supported by a Windows-container training platform.

name: PreAct: Computer-Using Agents that Get Faster on Repeated Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: PreAct compiles successful screen-interaction runs into guarded state-machine programs for repeated tasks. It validates programs from clean states before storage and returns control to the agent when replayed screen expectations fail, with tests across mobile, desktop and web.

name: Beyond the GUI Paradigm: Do Mobile Agents Need the Phone Screen?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: This study compares general coding agents using mobile command-line access with reproducible GUI agents on AndroidWorld and MobileWorld. It also supplies oracle CLI analyses and a separate task suite for operations such as bulk changes, filtering and hidden device state.

name: TUA-Bench: A Benchmark for General-Purpose Terminal-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent general computer-operation benchmark: the evaluated interface is a terminal; GUI benchmarks are a contrast, not its execution modality.
summary: TUA-Bench evaluates terminal-use agents on general digital tasks, including document editing, email, web information seeking and specialist software workflows. Tasks run in real terminals with deterministic setup and execution-based scoring.

name: LUMOS: A Semantic Operating-System Layer for Accessibility-Grounded AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: LUMOS converts native accessibility metadata and browser UI structure into semantic interface blueprints with stable element identifiers and available actions. It combines live pointer-to-element grounding with an observe-act loop constrained to visible-UI primitives.

name: Tactile: Giving Computer-Using Agents Hands and Feet
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Tactile turns accessibility, OCR and visual evidence into explicit desktop targets with executable actions and verification cues. Its execution loop chooses semantic actions or coordinate fallbacks while retaining provenance for replay and diagnosis.

name: MAGA: Multi-Platform Self-Fusion of GUI Agents via Structured Action Distillation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MAGA distills specialized GUI agents into one policy by allocating supervision according to structured-action correctness rather than treating all response tokens equally. A training-only teacher hint supports fusion across mobile, web and desktop settings without changing student inputs.

name: Activity Frames: Deterministic Screen-Activity Compilation for Agent Memory and Replay
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported capture analysis uses one professional's single-user corpus.
summary: Introduces Activity Frames, a deterministic pipeline that turns captured screen activity into typed episodes for computer-use agent memory and routine replay.

name: Back to the Future: A workbook time machine for spread sheet creation benchmarks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The benchmark covers formulas, charts, pivot tables, and conditional formatting in spreadsheets.

name: ASIL: Replacing Screenshot-and-Click with Structured State and Semantic Actions
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: ASIL exposes application state as structured JSON and provides code-executable semantic actions. Its application benchmark compares this interface with screenshot control and application-native APIs, and studies supervised and reinforcement learning on the structured interface.

name: UI-Venus-2 Technical Report
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Describes a GUI foundation agent trained through expanded environments, function-grounded tasks, and trajectory verification with safety-aware execution mechanisms.

name: OmegaUse-SOP: SOP Engineering for Professional Computer Use from Human Demonstrations
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: OmegaUse-SOP converts expert GUI demonstrations into configurable procedures and refines them with domain rules and human input. It records, abstracts, grounds and verifies live execution, with a case study of photovoltaic simulation workflows in PVsyst 7.2.

name: SCAFFOLD: Self-Improving Web Agents via Recursive Parametric Skill Abstraction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces SCAFFOLD, which extracts executable skills from web trajectories, composes them into a hierarchy, and compresses redundant skills through behavioral checks. It periodically distills skill-guided trajectories into the policy and studies repeated improvement across web benchmarks.

name: Improving Proficiency and Efficiency of Android GUI Agents via Self-Generating Tool Actions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: DroidTool generates application-state tools through proposal, implementation, testing and repair. Relational tests connect the tools’ preconditions and effects, and the resulting tools are evaluated as additions to Android GUI agents.

name: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: EchoPath turns validated GUI trajectories into parameterized replay procedures with explicit runtime preconditions. Image-based target matching adjusts stored coordinates, while ambiguous steps fall back to bounded repair or fresh planning.

name: PhoneCLI: From App Interfaces to Callable Commands for Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces PhoneCLI, which explores mobile app interfaces and compiles navigation paths into reusable commands without internal app APIs or instrumentation. At execution time it verifies compiled paths and falls back to a visual agent for open-ended interaction or failed navigation.

name: Neuro-Symbolic Computer Use: Learning Reusable Policies for Reliable and Efficient Execution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Learns reusable computer-use policies that encode stable workflow logic in programs while delegating grounding and state checks to neural models. Policy iteration executes variants, diagnoses failures, revises the program, and adds verification before state-changing actions.

name: GUI-HARVEST: Self-Improving GUI Agents through Evidence-Driven Harness Evolution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Improves GUI-agent execution code by analyzing action effects and repeated-task failures, then validating bounded changes with frozen model weights.

name: When to Compile a Computer-Use Agent? Measuring Payback and Making Compilation Decisions for Token Efficiency
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces PACE, a protocol and online decision rule for deciding when repeated GUI procedures are worth compiling into programs. It accounts for failed compilation attempts, measured per-use savings, uncertain reuse, and execution costs under an explicit cumulative budget.

name: Interaction-as-a-Judge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Uses computer-use agents to interact with generated applications, studying whether interaction improves preference judging, requirement checks, and feedback for application generation.

name: Step-Aligned Script Generation with Verification and Recovery for Web Automation Testing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports evaluation on three public web benchmarks.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Interface Quilt, which uses computer-use agents and generated UI overlays to modify how existing applications look and behave without source access.

name: FluidUse
notes: Published by FluidInference; the package targets macOS 14 or later. AccessibilityFormDriver snapshots the focused window of another running app through the macOS Accessibility API into form elements addressed by tokens, writes values through AXValue and presses buttons and checkboxes with AXPress; for Safari, Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, Firefox and similar browsers it sends real key events instead, because those apply AXValue writes to the focused field. WebFormDriver does the same for an embedded WKWebView through an injected script. FormSchema renders each field's context and a fixed option list (fill Label: value for each document entity, check, click, skip) for a model to score, and decodes the chosen option into an action. The README's form model is CUA-S1-FORMS, a 706K-parameter form specialist from Cua converted to Core ML; its manager (CuaS1FormsManager) comes from the FluidAudio package dependency, not from this tree. Most of the package consists of on-device Core ML runtimes for general typed-decision, classification, embedding and OCR models (laya, GLiNER 2.5, Kev, Clef, Intern-Decision, SigLIP2 and others) and demos such as Tetris and 2048 players, which do not operate GUIs. Latency and accuracy figures in the README are publisher measurements. Root LICENSE is Apache-2.0; not a fork, not archived; the latest release, v0.3.0, predates the inspected commit. Code was read, not run.
summary: Swift package for local computer use on Apple silicon that reads forms in running Mac apps or browsers through the Accessibility API and fills them with on-device Core ML decision models.

name: agent-computer-use
notes: Published on npm as agent-cu (package.json 0.1.1 at the inspected commit) with precompiled binaries, and also installable as an agent skill (skills/agent-computer-use/SKILL.md). Commands snapshot an app's accessibility tree into @eN refs or query it with a selector DSL (role, name, id, parent-child chains), then click, type, press keys, scroll, drag, move or resize windows, wait for elements, take screenshots, and run JSON batches or YAML workflows; output is JSON by default. Backends: macOS uses AXUIElement with CGEvent input, Windows uses UI Automation, and Linux uses AT-SPI2 over D-Bus with xdotool for input. Electron apps can be driven over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, but automatic Electron detection and relaunch with a debug port is implemented only on macOS (cli/crates/agent-computer-use-cdp/src/detect.rs). The README marks every platform as preview and states that the project is no longer maintained, recommending Cua Driver instead. The repository was formerly named kortix-ai/agent-click (same GitHub repository ID). The tool contains no model or agent loop. Code was read, not run.

notes: Next.js app run locally (version 0.4.1 in package.json; tag v0.4.1 points at b8016b5, and the inspected commit 489e9c4 is later). Each agent's workstation is a Docker container built from workstation/: Debian (trixie-slim) with Xvfb, xfwm4 and a panel, Chromium, x11vnc and noVNC, xdotool and scrot, a persistent home volume, and an inactivity watchdog. lib/agent/tools.ts defines the tool belt for the Vercel AI SDK streamText loop: shell and fs_* through docker exec; screen_capture and screen_share (scrot JPEG through xiryn-shot); pointer_click, pointer_move, pointer_drag, pointer_scroll, key_type and key_press (xdotool in lib/workstation.ts), each returning a fresh screenshot; request_takeover; vault_list, vault_fill, request_payment_approval and request_secret; memory_write and memory_forget; web_search and web_fetch through Firecrawl; and delegate for squads. Observation is plain screenshots of a 1280x800 display with pixel coordinates; there is no accessibility tree or element annotation. name: Roubao
notes: Kotlin Android app (minimum SDK 26) published by Turbo1123. Shizuku gives it ADB-level shell access without root, which DeviceController.kt uses for screencap, input tap/swipe/text and am start; the agent's floating overlay is hidden while each plain screenshot is taken. In the default mode MobileAgent.kt runs Manager (plan), Executor (one of click, double_tap, long_press, type, swipe, system_button, open_app, wait, take_over or answer, with pixel coordinates), ActionReflector (compares the before and after screenshots) and an optional Notetaker over an OpenAI-compatible VLM API, for at most 25 steps by default; the README calls this layer a Kotlin port of Mobile-Agent-v3. Two other modes call GUI-Owl through Alibaba Cloud DashScope's GUI agent endpoint (default model pre-gui_owl_7b), which returns actions directly, or an OpenAI-compatible MAI-UI server (default localhost:8000, MAI-UI-2B) with MAI-UI's prompt format and up to three history screenshots. A Skills layer (app/src/main/assets/skills.json) can instead hand a request to another app through a deep link, and Tools cover app search, deep links, clipboard, shell and HTTP. When screencap is blocked on a secure screen the agent asks the user before continuing; the Manager prompt stops the run when a screen actively asks for payment confirmation, a password or biometric verification, and the Executor can hand logins and captchas to the user (take_over) or ask for confirmation of payment actions. The README says a 2.0 version based on AccessibilityService is developed on a separate branch; this record describes main. Root LICENSE is MIT; not a fork, not archived; latest release V1.4.2. name: Webagent (webagent.cloud)
notes: Open-source code of the webagent.cloud hosted service, published by webagent-cloud. A FastAPI server (server.py, webagent/api.py) with a bundled React UI accepts a prompt and runs it with the engine set by ENGINE_PROVIDER: Browser Use by default, or Notte, whose agent is fixed to gemini-2.5-flash with at most 30 steps. The browser comes from BROWSER_PROVIDER: a local Playwright Chromium over CDP, Browserbase or Steel; at the reviewed commit the Steel provider's create_session takes a context argument that the caller does not pass. Models are reached through Browser Use's chat clients for OpenAI, DeepSeek, Anthropic, Google and Groq; other provider values fall back to the OpenAI client. After a run, workflow_builder_service.py asks an LLM to extract parameters from the prompt and template the recorded actions with their element XPaths; workflow_replay_service.py replays those steps with Playwright (navigation, search, XPath clicks and typing, scrolling, key presses, uploads, dropdowns) without a model and, when an action fails, hands that step to the AI engine for up to three attempts. Tasks, runs and results are kept in a local SQLite database; results can be text or JSON validated against a supplied JSON Schema, and a webhook can be called on completion. The README's n8n, Zapier and Make integrations and Stagehand engine are not in the tree. Root LICENSE is MIT; not a fork, not archived; no release. Code was read, not run.

notes: rabbit inc. lists r1 at $199 USD with no subscription. The r1 page and user guide place computer use in OS3 rather than on the device: OS3 works on computers where the rabbit agent is installed, through their terminal, and DLAM, which the guide calls rabbit's computer-use capability, drives an application's screen with the user's permission. The updates log dates a DLAM early-access preview for desktop control via r1 on Windows and Mac to 29 January 2026, BYOK support for DLAM with Anthropic and OpenAI keys to rabbitOS 2.3 (10 July 2026), and OS3 general availability to 22 September 2026. Earlier r1 releases shipped LAM playground, a web agent acting through a webdriver from visual and structured input (1 October 2024), and teach mode, which learned website tasks from demonstrations (21 November 2024); the current user guide describes neither. The DLAM model, its observations and its reliability were not independently tested.
summary: Pocket voice-and-touch AI device that serves as a physical channel into rabbit OS3, whose DLAM capability can drive applications on a computer the user connects, with permission.

name: CloudCruise
notes: The homepage targets payer-portal and EHR workflows and says every run executes in a VM with laptop-like fingerprints and human-like input, with queued concurrency, video replay, per-action screenshots and logs, and HIPAA-compliant infrastructure. The documentation says the builder agent opens a live browser preview, navigates the target site, asks clarifying questions and turns confirmed actions into a node-and-edge graph that later runs deterministically instead of calling an LLM at every step. Click nodes target elements either by XPath or through an LLM vision mode labelled AI (Screenshot). The maintenance agent classifies failures from the error screenshot, page state and selector signals, then recovers in place, asks for input, retries or hands the workflow to the builder agent. Citrix virtual desktops are automated through their HTML5 browser client using the screenshot mode. Runs start through an API with TypeScript and Python SDKs. Pricing and reliability were not independently tested.
summary: Managed browser-automation platform for healthcare portals and EHRs in which a builder agent turns a chat description into a reusable workflow graph that runs in cloud VMs and a maintenance agent repairs.

name: Tongyi UI Agent API
notes: The page (version V0.0.1) documents a DashScope endpoint for the gui-owl app that takes a screenshot URL, a task instruction, a session ID and optional operation hints (add_info), and returns the next action, such as a click or swipe with screen coordinates, with a thought and an explanation. Requests set device_type to mobile or pc and use the model pre-gui_owl_7b; the PC pipeline also names worker, manager, reflector and notetaker models and can enable the reflection and memory agents. The page states that the agent targets phones, in-car systems, TVs and PCs, names no mobile operating system, and lists usage as free for a limited time. The X-PLUG/MobileAgent README links this page as a limited-time free Mobile-Agent-v3 API; the page itself names no paper or released checkpoint, so no relation to the Mobile-Agent or GUI-Owl records is asserted. The receipt uses the Markdown export because the HTML embeds a per-request tracking ID.
summary: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio API that returns the next GUI action with its reasoning for a screenshot and task, with a mobile pipeline and a PC pipeline using planner, worker, reflector and memory agents.

name: Yutori
notes: Yutori was founded by Abhishek Das, Devi Parikh and Dhruv Batra and announced its seed round in March 2025. Navigator models are called through an OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible endpoint: the caller sends a screenshot and a task, the model returns actions as tool calls, and the caller executes them and sends a fresh screenshot in an agent loop. n1.5 drives browsers in a normalized 1000x1000 coordinate space with a core set of 18 coordinate-based tools or an expanded set that adds element extraction, find, set_element_value and JavaScript execution, and can return JSON matching a caller schema. n2 operates a full desktop through batched GUI actions plus bash and file tools; the SDK ships local Docker and Daytona examples, and Yutori MCP runs it on the visible macOS desktop, sending screen contents to Yutori. A Python SDK wraps the APIs, a CLI runs research, browsing and Scout tasks, and an MCP server with workflow skills exposes these tasks and computer use to coding agents. Scouts monitor the web on a schedule, and Delegate is a consumer agent meant to complete handed-off tasks independently. Yutori also publishes a computer-use leaderboards page compiling reported results for six benchmarks. The publisher describes its Online-Mind2Web figure as independently verified and its Navi-Bench v2 and Westworld figures as its own evaluations; capabilities, pricing and reliability were not independently tested.
summary: Yutori's web-agent platform: the Navigator computer-use model API (n1.5 for browsers, n2 for full desktops), task APIs for browsing, research and Scout web monitoring, and the Delegate personal agent.
